_doc: Questions a coding or research agent asks about this project. gold: strings that must all appear (case-insensitive) in the context the agent read for it to be answerable. gold_files: what an oracle would open (repo-relative, or vault:<note path>). category: code | vault | cross | stale (stale = the answer lives in a file the index has not been re-synced with; measures the cost of an out-of-date index).

questions.question: How is an episode id derived, and why does a document keep its identity across edits?
questions.gold_answer: file_id = uuid5 of tenant|source|external_id; episode_id = uuid5 of file_id plus sha1 of the text. A document is a container that is revised, so its id is stable; an episode is content, so its id changes with the text.

questions.question: What happens in the chains stage when no call finishes for the stall timeout?
questions.gold_answer: The remaining calls are abandoned: a warning is printed, the HTTP client is closed so parked threads error out, and the generator ends; callers must treat those items as not done.

questions.question: Why is cannot_link off by default in the linker, and what did it score?
questions.gold_answer: Blocking merges across explicit splits scored 0.774 CoNLL against 0.945 for plain union-find on the same decisions, so the constraint is off by default.

questions.question: Which surfaces become rows in the surfaces table, and why are pronouns kept out?
questions.gold_answer: Only identifying surfaces are rows. A pronoun is how the model linked mentions, not a name; stored, it would become a seed matching every question.

questions.question: What do connector keys settle for a candidate pair (keys_settle)?
questions.gold_answer: Two chains with different connector keys are two things, and a keyed chain beside an unkeyed one is a symbol beside prose; such pairs are not sent to the reviewer.

questions.question: Why is the context vector left uncentered in the linker?
questions.gold_answer: Episode-centering removes the episode's shared component and the entity's own signal with it: centered AUC 0.505, uncentered 0.898.

questions.question: How is a chain's head chosen when the model's head choice does not survive validation?
questions.gold_answer: It falls back within the chain: proper name, then definite description, then the longest span, rather than discarding the chain.

questions.question: What are the steps the Slack ingress performs on an incoming event, in order?
questions.gold_answer: Verify the signature on the raw bytes, dedupe, ACK within the budget, then answer in the thread from a background task.

questions.question: What did the vector cache measure for a nomic forward pass and the model load?
questions.gold_answer: A forward pass costs 63 ms per episode plus a 14.5 s model load, against 11 ms to reload the cache file, so a re-link over an unchanged corpus skips every pass.

questions.question: In incremental linking, which pairs get re-scored?
questions.gold_answer: Only pairs that could have changed: those touching a chain not linked last time, and old pairs whose chains share a surface with a new one.

questions.question: What resource ceilings do the login roles carry?
questions.gold_answer: statement_timeout 30s and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 10s, set on the login roles because per-role settings are not inherited.

questions.question: Which database role claims a tenant and which one derives it?
questions.gold_answer: app_ingest claims a tenant (uploads, backfills); app_connector derives it from the connector and workspace id and cannot claim one.

questions.question: When does merge_seeded fold a model chain into a seed?
questions.gold_answer: When a model span touches a seed span: the same offsets or the same text, whatever the parser typed it as.

questions.question: Why are the span ids returned by the coreference model validated?
questions.gold_answer: Ids not issued are a protocol violation: UnknownSpanIds is raised, the caller retries once, then fails the episode. Ids instead of generated text are only worth anything if checked.

questions.question: How does strip_markup treat wiki link targets?
questions.gold_answer: Wiki link targets survive as plain text, because [[Potential Markets]] is a deliberate reference and one of the few cross-document signals a vault gives.

questions.question: Why does ANN blocking use the name vector rather than the context vector?
questions.gold_answer: The name vector measured AUC 0.98+ for identity while the context vector reaches 0.745, so neighbours in name space are the ones worth examining.

questions.question: Why are episodes scored by the mean of their ranked entities rather than sum or max?
questions.gold_answer: max ties every episode holding the top entity and sum rewards long notes; on the vault the answering notes ranked 25th under sum, 10th under max, 7th under mean.

questions.question: How does the condense step turn a thread follow-up into a standalone question?
questions.gold_answer: A gpt-4.1-mini call rewrites the latest message as a standalone question and returns needs_lookup, false for acknowledgements and rewrites.

questions.question: Why is Neo4j unscalable for us and what is the alternative?
questions.gold_answer: Neo4j's linear per-tenant pricing forces a silo per customer; the alternative is Supabase with shared infrastructure (bridge or pool model).

questions.question: What is the pool model?
questions.gold_answer: A fully shared database with a single schema where data is separated by a tenant_id column or row-level security; what we have now.

questions.question: Which companies should we sell to first?
questions.gold_answer: Startups that have just raised seed or Series A and want growth: they explore, use AI tools heavily, and can take the product as an MCP tool.

questions.question: Why was HDBSCAN preferred over correlation clustering?
questions.gold_answer: HDBSCAN is more stable, gives denser clusters and can map out noise (singleton concepts), though unstable while clusters are small.

questions.question: What did the context span mean pooling hypothesis get wrong?
questions.gold_answer: It embeds the general episode context rather than the entity, because it attends to the whole episode, so it is a bad predictor of identity across documents.

questions.question: Why does RLS beat a WHERE clause in each query?
questions.gold_answer: A WHERE in each query is N places to make a mistake; RLS bound to the schema is one place, easier to manage and more restrictive.

questions.question: How are entity edges derived in the query data flow?
questions.gold_answer: By a self-join of chains on episode_id, PMI-weighted; the edges are derived, not stored, and feed PPR.

questions.question: What is the largest remaining security item after the schema work?
questions.gold_answer: Cloud Tasks OIDC on the worker endpoint: everything in the wall trusts that app.workspace_id is genuine.

questions.question: How do the three app roles differ in what they can claim?
questions.gold_answer: app_connector derives the tenant from connector plus workspace and cannot claim one; app_ingest claims a tenant for uploads; app_ack only inserts events and reads nothing.

questions.question: What connection limits and statement timeouts do the roles have?
questions.gold_answer: Statement timeouts 30s/30s/5s and connection limits 30/10/40 for connector, ingest and ack.
